name: Ban'ethil Barrow Den
summary: Beneath Teldrassil's roots, Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den. The sacred chambers were made for the sleeping Druids of the Talon, whose spirits commune with the Emerald Dream. Now the den is a dangerous warren, and the druids within are at risk.

sections.title: A Defiled Sanctuary
sections.body: Ban'ethil Barrow Den lies beneath Teldrassil's roots, with chambers above and below. Barrow dens shelter night elf druids as they sleep and send their spirits into the Emerald Dream. This den was made for the Druids of the Talon to commune with nature. Its halls once held quiet meditation, but corruption spreading through Teldrassil's wildlife reached the Gnarlpine furbolgs. They invaded and made the hollowed chambers a fortified warren.

sections.title: The Gnarlpine Incursion
sections.body: The Gnarlpine tribe has gone mad under a mysterious corruption spreading across the World Tree. Its furbolgs drove out or endangered the sleeping druids, and now guard the winding tunnels fiercely. Any night elf who approaches is attacked. Teldrassil's defenders must drive the furbolgs back to protect the vulnerable druids and the sacred relics trapped in the den's lower depths.

faq.answer: Ban'ethil Barrow Den is a hollow beneath Teldrassil, made by night elves to shelter the sleeping Druids of the Talon. As they sleep, their spirits roam the Emerald Dream.

faq.q: Why are there furbolgs inside Ban'ethil Barrow Den?
faq.answer: The Gnarlpine furbolgs fell to a spreading corruption among Teldrassil's creatures. They turned hostile, invaded the den, displaced its keepers, and now threaten the sleeping druids.

faq.q: What are the sections of the barrow den?
faq.answer: The den has two connected tiers. The Upper Den lies near the entrance passages, while the Lower Den reaches deeper among the subterranean roots.

faq.q: Why are barrow dens so important to druids?
aliases: why do druids sleep in barrows
faq.answer: Barrow dens shelter druids whose deep sleep lets their consciousness enter the Emerald Dream. Their waking bodies lie helpless for years or decades, so they need safe and secure shelter.

angles.text: As a druid, you can see Ban'ethil as sacred ground for the Cenarion Circle. It was built to protect the Druids of the Talon as they commune with the Emerald Dream.
As a night elf, you can see the Gnarlpine occupation of Ban'ethil as a warning of the sickness spreading through your new home, Teldrassil.
